overview:
California's 38th District is an open seat after redistricting, and Democrats hold a clear structural advantage here. The district leans Democratic by about 8 points, and the national environment adds further to that edge. Hilda Solis, a well-known local official, has raised more than $1 million and benefits from outside spending, while Republican Pedro Casas reports no fundraising or cash on hand.

No public polls cover the race, and no expert raters have weighed in, so the forecast rests on fundamentals and money. Prediction markets price the Democratic candidate at roughly 98 percent. The expected margin is about 20 points, consistent with a Safe Democratic rating, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
